searchText: CL call in 9.5 hours https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/475 first portion dedicated to Kiln discussions In EL The Merge is called "Merge". Will it stay this way? https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/master/network-upgrades/mainnet-upgrades/merge.md There's a current naming thread: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/el-merge-client-release-naming/7928 And here's the previous one from half a year ago: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/ethereum-roadmapping-improvements/6653/12 IMHO either Serenity or Merge is fine https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-1482-define-a-maximum-block-timestamp-drift/1556 This old-ish EIP states that the limits are already in place in geth: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/consensus/ethash/consensus.go#L46 and https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/consensus/ethash/consensus.go#L270 The motivation stated in the EIP still makes a lot of sense. cc <@!211091239112671234> <@!583892532644151312> Yeah, I expect in the next couple weeks it probably makes sense to settle on a name, like CL folks did with Bellatrix 🙂 I think the pushback on Serenity is that it was meant as including both PoS and scalability/sharding, and the merge is only the former. The challenge with « merge » is that it describes the entire process across both CL + EL, so having a more specific name for the client releases which are merge-compatible is useful It is definitely useful and actually it doesn't matter that much which exact name it will be (as for me) In that case, no need to join the (future) breakout room debating it 😁 was there ever a reason docking fell out of favour relative to merge? (to me) the former feels applicable to a (small subset such as a) single block within the wider merge process The actual transition happens a bit after software with implementation of Merge EIPs is released including TTD in its binary distribution. And as i understand we need a name for this release. Not sure if docking would be a good one for it. I personally like devcon cities but Shanghai is already booked for the first hardfork after the Merge IIUC I would expect it's because there's a slang meaning for that term. I think it can still be Shanghai Could be Amsterdam too, as it is similarly filling the gap between devcons 😅 <timbeiko> Someone suggested Paris (EthCC) for this reason, and as a way to highlight the broader community - I like that 🙂 (re @allcoredevs_bot: <Alex (axic)>Could be Amsterdam too, as it is similarly filling the gap between devcons 😅) That also sounds interesting. Timeline wise the first one was edcon not ethcc yet (and iirc it came after Shanghai) :) <timbeiko> ohh, where was the first edcon? Paris <timbeiko> lmao <timbeiko> guess it makes that choice easy 🙂

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: Yeah, I expect in the next couple weeks it probably makes sense to settle on a name, like CL folks did with Bellatrix 🙂

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: I think the pushback on Serenity is that it was meant as including both PoS and scalability/sharding, and the merge is only the former. The challenge with « merge » is that it describes the entire process across both CL + EL, so having a more specific name for the client releases which are merge-compatible is useful
